questions.prompt: A user has Contributor at subscription scope and Reader on rg-app inside that subscription. No deny, condition, policy, or lock blocks an operation. Can the user manage resources in rg-app?

options.explanation: The child Reader grant does not subtract inherited permissions.

options.text: No, because the most specific Reader grant replaces Contributor.
options.explanation: Azure RBAC grants are additive, not most-specific-role wins.

options.text: Only if Contributor was assigned more recently.
options.explanation: Assignment time is not the deciding precedence.

options.text: Only if Owner is also assigned on every resource.
options.explanation: Contributor already supplies the relevant management grant.

questions.prompt: A user has Owner on vm-app. An applicable deny assignment blocks only virtual-machine deletion for that user on vm-app; it does not deny configuration reads. No other restriction applies. Which pair of RBAC outcomes should the administrator expect?

options.text: Reading configuration is allowed; deleting the VM is blocked.
options.explanation: Owner grants both actions, but the matching deletion deny blocks that operation while leaving reads permitted.

options.text: Reading configuration and deleting the VM are both allowed.
options.explanation: Owner does not override an applicable deny assignment on deletion.

options.text: Reading configuration and deleting the VM are both blocked.
options.explanation: The deny is limited to deletion; it does not block the granted read operation.

options.text: Reading configuration is blocked; deleting the VM is allowed.
options.explanation: This reverses the stated deny scope: deletion is denied and reads are not.

questions.prompt: User1 can read vm-app configuration even though no Azure role is assigned directly to User1 at that VM. Which two assignment paths could each independently supply this current access? Select two.

options.text: An active Reader assignment directly to User1 at the containing subscription.
options.explanation: The subscription grant is inherited by vm-app and permits configuration reads.

options.text: An active Reader assignment on vm-app to a security group containing User1.
options.explanation: The group grant supplies Reader permissions to its member at the VM scope.

options.text: An active Reader assignment to User1 on a different VM in the same resource group.
options.explanation: Resource-scope permission does not extend to a sibling VM.

options.text: An eligible Reader assignment for User1 on vm-app that has not been activated.
options.explanation: Eligibility must be activated before it provides current role permissions.
